1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Harlow Bay International is a mid-sized fictional airport. Its baggage handling system and manual encode desk are run by the Harlow Bay Airport Authority (HBAA). Corvane Air is the largest carrier at the station. On 1 September Corvane's ramp handling, and Pelion Airways' ramp handling, moved from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground. Departing bags pass through automatic tag reader arrays. Bags whose tags cannot be read are diverted to a manual encode desk and then sent on to the make-up laterals, where handler crews load carts that close 35 minutes before departure.
9	Your request: Corvane's VP Ground Operations plans to issue Tessaly Ground a formal breach notice this Friday. Before that, the steering group has asked you to work out why Corvane's departing-bag mishandling rate at Harlow Bay nearly doubled from September and to recommend what to do next.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Corvane Air station performance dashboard, Harlow Bay, extract dated 4 Nov (system-record): Departing bags not carried on the booked flight, per 1,000 departing passengers: Jun 4.0, Jul 4.1, Aug 4.1, Sep 7.6, Oct 7.9. Departing passengers: Jun 205,000; Jul 212,000; Aug 219,000; Sep 188,000; Oct 176,000. Corvane network average excluding Harlow Bay: between 3.9 and 4.2 in every month. On-time departures within 15 minutes: Aug 81%, Sep 77%, Oct 78%. Annotation by station office: 'Ground handling transferred from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground, 1 Sep.' No other annotations on the dashboard.
12	- Email from Dana Orlov, Corvane Station Manager, to Martin Achterberg, 5 Nov (manager-account): Martin, the rate sat at about 4 for over a year under Quillon and nearly doubled the month Tessaly took over. Their crews are green. I have personally watched bags sitting on a lateral with nobody working the cart. Tessaly keep blaming 'the airport system' and the encode desk, but that is the same desk Quillon worked with for six years without complaint. The two new evening departures add some pressure, but we ran heavier banks every summer. I recommend a formal breach notice and withholding the performance element of the fee until the rate is back under 4.5. Dana
13	- Tessaly Ground monthly staffing return to Corvane, 31 Oct (document): Harlow Bay ramp headcount: 164 (contract minimum 160). Staff with under six months' airside experience: 67 (41%). Comparator from Quillon's final return, 31 Aug: headcount 152, of whom 18 (12%) had under six months. 23 former Quillon loaders transferred to Tessaly. Shift fill rate, Sep–Oct: early 97%, late 94%, evening 89%. Crewing model: a single Harlow Bay crew pool covers all Tessaly-handled turns (Corvane Air and Pelion Airways), assigned by the shift lead. Tessaly also staffs Corvane's baggage service desk under the same contract.
14	- Minutes, Corvane–Tessaly weekly operations review, 29 Oct (document): Present: D. Orlov (Corvane), P. Venn (Tessaly ops lead), two Corvane duty managers. HBAA was invited but did not attend. 1. Mishandling: P. Venn said 'a lot of our late bags come down from the manual encode station after the lateral has closed' and asked Corvane to raise encode delays with HBAA. D. Orlov replied that the encode desk is unchanged and that crews should sweep laterals before closing carts. 2. Schedule: Corvane 418 and Corvane 422 added to the evening bank from 1 Sep; no change to lateral closing times. 3. Actions: Tessaly to submit a crew retraining plan by 12 Nov; Corvane to circulate the October dashboard.
15	- Corvane IT helpdesk ticket summary, bag-tag printers, Harlow Bay, 1 Aug–31 Oct (log): Weekly tickets categorised 'tag printer jam/misfeed' (kiosks and counters combined): August weekly average 5; September–October weekly average 13. Context notes appended by helpdesk: (a) Procurement (L. Sato): from 1 Sep all Harlow Bay counters and kiosks switched from Brackwater Print tag stock to Fennick Labels stock under a new contract, unit cost down 18%. The Brackwater contract remains valid to 31 Dec, and about five weeks of Brackwater stock is held in station stores. (b) The kiosk maintenance vendor moved kiosk printer preventive cleaning from weekly to fortnightly from 1 Sep; counter printers are maintained by Corvane IT, schedule unchanged. (c) No printer configuration changes recorded since June.
16	- Message from Martin Achterberg, Corvane VP Ground Operations, to the Harlow Bay steering group, 6 Nov (leadership-account): I've read Dana's note and I agree with it. We changed one thing on 1 September, the handler, and the mishandling rate nearly doubled. Tessaly bid low, staffed up with new hires, and is now pointing at the airport's IT. I want a breach notice drafted for my signature by Friday and the performance payment held. If anyone has evidence that this is not a handling problem, bring it to me before then. Otherwise we proceed.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	Don't send the breach notice. The rise in lost bags comes from tag-reading failures, not from the handler change. Since 1 September, tags printed on the new Fennick stock fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against 1.5% before. Pelion and transfer tags stayed near 1.3–1.4%. The failed bags go to the manual encode desk, where evening waits grew from 7 to about 30 minutes, and most of those bags then reach the lateral after it closes. Bags on the auto-read path are unchanged. Pelion, which uses the same Tessaly crews, is flat. That argues strongly against crew inexperience as the main driver. A natural test on 14–16 October backs this up. Counters that used old Brackwater stock failed at 1.6%, while kiosks on Fennick stock still failed at 12%. Next steps: put counters and kiosks back on Brackwater stock now. About five weeks of it is in stores and the contract runs to 31 December. Hold the breach notice and fee withholding. Have Fennick and the printer maker work out whether the fault is the stock itself or the printer heat setting before you lodge any defect claim. Asking the airport authority for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap. I am fairly confident, but jam tickets and the cause inside the Fennick problem are unproven.
20
